title: P02 follow-up: raise decoupled weight decay on the Muon matrices from 3x to 10x (MUON_WD 0.03 -> 0.1) on the 069 incumbent
description: P02 follow-up (Muon weight decay, continuing 069-claude's 1x->3x keep): the only edit raises the Muon group's decoupled weight decay from 3x to 10x the AdamW per-step shrinkage (MUON_WD 0.03 -> 0.1; peak per-step shrinkage 3e-4 -> 1e-3), leaving the AdamW group, LRs, batch, schedule and init identical to incumbent 069-claude. 069's gain arrived late in expert iteration (RL-solved +19/+27/+20 on every seed with unchanged val loss), which fits smaller Muon weights being more plastic under the frozen RL AdamW; this tests whether that trend continues or whether stronger shrinkage starts to cost attention sharpness.
hypothesis: Muon adds updates of fixed spectral size, so hidden-weight norms are set by the balance of update size and decay (consistently aligned directions reach spectral scale ~1/wd; noise directions ~sqrt(lr/(2 wd)) per unit update). The frozen RL AdamW takes steps of roughly fixed per-element size, so its relative step is ~lr_RL/||W||: smaller pretrained Muon weights let expert iteration move the model further per round. 069 (3x decay, cumulative factor 0.46) left val loss unchanged but raised round-4 sample accuracy and RL-solved on every seed, the plasticity signature. 10x decay (time constant ~1000 steps, cumulative factor ~0.07) should shrink noise-driven weight mass further while the needed directions stay at spectral scale ~10, enough for attention sharpness because LayerNorm gains (AdamW, unchanged) can compensate for scale. If the equilibrium weights are too small for sharp citation attention, pretraining fit worsens and RL starts from a weaker policy: the risk this test measures.
expected_delta: -60 to +30 theorems at >=7 (central guess -5); pretraining final val loss within +0.01 of 069's 0.0923/0.0914/0.0967 (a rise beyond that signals the sharpness failure mode); if plasticity continues, RL-solved above 069's 762/743/792 on at least two of three seeds

arch.change: none versus 069-claude: 5 untied fork GPT blocks, d_model 256, 8 heads (head dim 32), d_ff 1024, RoPE base 10000, LayerNorm, GELU, untied embedding/readout
arch.checkpoint_reconstruction: GPT(vocab, 5, 256, 8) from the fork; model.cfg records n_layer=5 and the state dict has blocks.0-blocks.4
arch.kv_cache: one fork KV-cache dict per logical block (5 per sample), unchanged fork code

optimizer.name: split-QKV Muon on hidden matrices and the output readout head.weight throughout; continuous AdamW auxiliary (unchanged from 069-claude except Muon weight decay)

muon.precision: bf16 Newton-Schulz; fp32 momentum and parameters
muon.shape_scale: sqrt(max(1, rows/columns)) per orthogonalized matrix: Q/K/V each 1, attention output 1, fc1 2, fc2 1, head (99,256) 1
muon.schedule: same warmup/cosine fraction as AdamW; muon_lr = 0.01 * adam_lr / 0.001
muon.parameters: All 20 hidden projection parameters (4 per block x 5 blocks) plus head.weight (99,256; vocab 99, no bias) are in Muon: 21 matrices. Five qkv.weight matrices of shape (768,256) use independent Q/K/V updates, represented as a batch of three (256,256) matrices; proj/fc1/fc2 and head are orthogonalized whole. head is wide (99<256) so it is not transposed and its update has 99 singular values near 1.
muon.license: MIT; full copyright and permission notice retained in pretrain.py
muon.qkv_split: After elementwise Nesterov momentum, reshape each QKV update to (3,256,256); independently Frobenius-normalize and run five batched Newton-Schulz steps; reshape back before applying. No extra learning-rate multiplier. Momentum and weight decay stay elementwise and unchanged.

optimizer.adamw_parameters: emb.weight, all projection biases and LayerNorm parameters (incl. ln_f) throughout; head.weight and hidden matrices never enter pretraining AdamW
optimizer.decay_convention: CHANGED: MUON_WD = 10 * WD * LR / MUON_LR = 0.1 (069-claude: 3x = 0.03), so Muon lr*0.1 is ten times the auxiliary AdamW lr*0.1 per-step shrinkage at every schedule fraction (peak 1e-3 per step instead of 3e-4; decay time constant ~1000 steps at peak LR instead of ~3.3k). Applies to all 21 Muon matrices including head.weight. AdamW group decay (wd 0.1 at lr 1e-3) is unchanged. Summed over ~4750 steps (mean schedule factor ~0.55) the cumulative multiplicative decay factor is ~exp(-2.6)=0.07 instead of ~exp(-0.79)=0.46, so the orthogonal init is mostly forgotten and weight norms sit near the decay/update equilibrium by the end of pretraining.
optimizer.clipping: joint global gradient norm 1.0 before both optimizers
optimizer.handoff: standard GPT weights only; pretraining optimizer states are discarded and frozen RL creates its own unchanged AdamW

config.init: Exactly 069-claude: fork default construction with 5 blocks, then orthogonal_ on every 2D block parameter (gain 0.02*sqrt(max(rows, cols))); embedding and readout keep the fork normal(0.02); biases zero. Initial weights and data order/shift RNG streams per seed identical to 069-claude.
